message.reasoning: We need to navigate to temporary directory. In this environment, we don't know the path. Usually /tmp. We can use pwd to see current. Then cd? There's no cd tool. But we can use ls with path? The ls tool only lists current directory. We can use find? But we need to navigate. There's no tool to change directory. Maybe we can use pwd to see current. Then we can use ls with path? The ls tool signature: ls({a?: boolean}). It doesn't accept path. So we can't list arbitrary directory. But maybe we can use find with path? find can search under a path. So we can use find with path="/tmp" and name=None to list all. That will return list of files and directories. But the user wants to list all files in temporary directory including hidden. find will include hidden? It will search recursively. But we want just top-level? They said "navigate to the temporary directory and list all the files available there right in the terminal for me? I would like to quickly skim through them and all the hidden files." So we need to list all files in /tmp including hidden. We can use find with path="/tmp" and name=None. That will list all items recursively. But maybe we want just top-level. We can use find with path="/tmp" and name=None and then filter? But we can just output the result. Let's do find.
